purpose: Fixes 15 code quality audit findings: removes Phase 2 comments, migrates console.log to winston, adds future-date event validation, introduces whyVolunteer deprecation pattern with backward compatibility, fixes unsafe Prisma cast, consolidates imports, and denormalizes totalHours to User for leaderboard performance.
riskRationale: All changes are backwards-compatible with dual-write/dual-field migration patterns. A migration with proper backfill queries is included. No breaking API changes. The pre-existing hours-calculation bug in approveAttendance is replicated but not introduced by this PR.

text: Well-structured PR that cleanly addresses all 15 audit findings. The totalHours denormalization correctly uses dual-writes and includes a migration with backfill queries. The whyVoluntary→whyVolunteer deprecation uses a safe dual-field input pattern. The CreateEventSchema/EventSchema split with future-date validation is clean. A pre-existing hours-calculation bug is replicated to User.totalHours and test coverage for the new schema is missing, but these are additive improvements rather than regressions.

reasoning: The migration already exists with proper backfill queries (confirmed by batch 5 review). Remaining issues are minor (stale types, dead mock data, missing comment) or pre-existing (hours-calculation bug in approveAttendance). The missing test coverage for the new validation schema is additive work. No regressions introduced.

message: The flatMap pattern correctly expands each hour adjustment into a pair of writes (VolunteerProfile + User) within a single transaction, maintaining atomicity for the dual-write migration.

The addEventRefinements function composes shared validation rules (meeting link for virtual, end time after start time) across both CreateEventSchema and EventSchema, preventing drift between create and update schemas.
The 5-second grace period on future-date validation is a pragmatic guard against clock drift and rapid form submission, with an explanatory comment — exactly the right level of detail.
Replacing as never with Parameters<typeof prisma.$on>[0] is a proper type-safe approach that leverages TypeScript's utility types instead of silencing the type checker.
The deprecation warning for whyVoluntary at usage-time is well-placed — it logs when old clients use the deprecated field without breaking them, giving ops visibility into migration progress.
The migration includes proper backfill queries — copying existing totalHours from VolunteerProfile and whyVoluntary into the new fields, preventing data loss.

A pre-existing hours-calculation bug in approveAttendance is replicated to User.totalHours. The rawHours recalculation at approval time caps at 16h while checkout capped at scheduledHours, causing incorrect adjustments when approvedHours equals scheduled hours. This bug pre-dates the PR but is now dual-written to both fields.
suggestion: Fix the hoursDiff calculation to cap at the same scheduledHours used at checkout time, so the adjustment is correct regardless of the 16h default cap.

message: CreateEventSchema future-date validation is untested. This is business-critical logic that prevents creation of past-dated events, and has no test coverage.
suggestion: Add unit tests for CreateEventSchema that verify: (1) future dates pass, (2) past dates (>5s ago) fail, (3) edge conditions near the grace period boundary.

message: The addEventRefinements function doesn't validate that meetingLink should be absent when isVirtual is false. A client could send a meetingLink for an in-person event and it would be silently stored.
suggestion: Add a .refine to reject meetingLink when isVirtual is false, to maintain data integrity and prevent misleading data.

message: The controller writes whyVoluntary (the deprecated field) to the database alongside whyVolunteer with the same value. Writing to a deprecated field defeats the purpose of deprecation — it should only write to whyVolunteer and stop populating whyVoluntary.
suggestion: Remove the whyVoluntary write on line 88 — only write whyVolunteer to the database. The deprecated field only needs to be accepted on input for backwards compatibility, not stored.

message: BatchData.profile type still declares totalHours: number, but the query at line 64 no longer selects it. While nothing reads profile.totalHours anymore (all criteria migrated to user.totalHours), the stale type is misleading for developers.
suggestion: Remove totalHours from the profile type in BatchData since it's no longer selected by the query.
suggestionCode: profile: { bio: string | null; currentStreak: number } | null;

message: Multiple test mocks for volunteerProfile.findUnique still include totalHours even though the badge engine no longer reads totalHours from volunteerProfile. These are dead mock values — harmless but misleading and could mask future refactoring errors.
suggestion: Remove the totalHours property from volunteerProfile.findUnique mock return values throughout the test file since the service no longer reads it from the profile.

message: EventSeriesSchema duplicates the HH:MM time comparison logic from addEventRefinements. The same minute-calculation (endH * 60 + endM > startH * 60 + startM) appears verbatim in both places, creating a risk of divergence.
suggestion: Extract the time comparison to a shared utility function used by both addEventRefinements and EventSeriesSchema to avoid drift between the two implementations.

message: The composite index @@index([points, totalHours]) helps points-sorted queries but the hours-sorted leaderboard query (orderBy: { totalHours: 'desc' }) would benefit from a standalone index on totalHours alone.
suggestion: Add @@index([totalHours]) for the hours-sorted query path.

message: VolunteerProfile.totalHours still exists alongside User.totalHours. The dual-field approach works but the deprecated field should eventually be removed to prevent confusion.
suggestion: Add an explicit comment that VolunteerProfile.totalHours should be removed in a future migration once all read paths are confirmed to use User.totalHours exclusively. Consider also extracting the grace period into a named constant.
